Container.Name: tModLoader-Web-Managed-Server
Container.Overview:
Independently maintained Terraria tModLoader dedicated server with a web dashboard for worlds, Workshop mods, players, configuration, and backups. Inspired by JACOBSMILE/tmodloader1.4. First startup requires internet access to install the game runtime. Open the container logs for the one-time setup code, then open WebUI and create your administrator credential. The game waits for setup. Manage game settings in the dashboard after setup; saved dashboard settings take precedence over environment defaults. Use dedicated data and backup folders; startup repairs their ownership to UID/GID 1000:1000. Keep the dashboard on a trusted LAN or use an HTTPS reverse proxy.
Wiki guides: Dashboard setup: https://github.com/Crosis47/tmodloader/wiki/Web-Dashboard#access-and-credentials Settings ownership: https://github.com/Crosis47/tmodloader/wiki/Configuration#choose-who-manages-settings Networking and proxy access: https://github.com/Crosis47/tmodloader/wiki/Networking-and-Access Storage and updates: https://github.com/Crosis47/tmodloader/wiki/Updates-and-Storage Worlds and Journey mode: https://github.com/Crosis47/tmodloader/wiki/Worlds-and-Playthroughs Mods and Workshop: https://github.com/Crosis47/tmodloader/wiki/Mods-and-Workshop Backups and recovery: https://github.com/Crosis47/tmodloader/wiki/Backups-and-Recovery Autosave and restart schedules: https://github.com/Crosis47/tmodloader/wiki/Configuration#scheduling All settings and defaults: https://github.com/Crosis47/tmodloader/wiki/Configuration#defaults-reference Troubleshooting: https://github.com/Crosis47/tmodloader/wiki/Troubleshooting

Config.Name: Game port
Config.Description: Host TCP port players connect to. Keep the container port at 7777. || Wiki: https://github.com/Crosis47/tmodloader/wiki/Networking-and-Access#game-connections

Config.Name: Dashboard port
Config.Description: Host dashboard port. Keep the container port at 8080; the WebUI button follows this mapping. || Wiki: https://github.com/Crosis47/tmodloader/wiki/Networking-and-Access#change-the-dashboard-port

Config.Name: Server data
Config.Description: Dedicated folder for worlds, mods, runtime, dashboard credentials, settings, and logs. Startup sets ownership to 1000:1000. || Wiki: https://github.com/Crosis47/tmodloader/wiki/Updates-and-Storage#persistent-folders

Config.Name: Backup archives
Config.Description: Dedicated backup folder. Preserve this and server data during updates. Startup sets ownership to 1000:1000. || Wiki: https://github.com/Crosis47/tmodloader/wiki/Updates-and-Storage#persistent-folders

Config.Name: Manage game settings with
Config.Description: web: saved dashboard values override Unraid game settings; Unraid values only seed unsaved settings. env: Unraid controls game settings and dashboard configuration editing is disabled. Dashboard disabled always uses env. || Wiki: https://github.com/Crosis47/tmodloader/wiki/Configuration#choose-who-manages-settings

Config.Name: Use custom server configuration
Config.Description: Yes requires TMOD_CONFIG_SOURCE=env or dashboard disabled, plus a separately added read-only file mapping to /terraria-server/customconfig.txt. Keep its game port at 7777 for this template. || Wiki: https://github.com/Crosis47/tmodloader/wiki/Configuration#custom-server-configuration

Config.Name: Dashboard origin
Config.Description: Leave empty for server-IP access. For a hostname or proxy, enter the exact browser origin including scheme and non-default port. || Wiki: https://github.com/Crosis47/tmodloader/wiki/Configuration#web-dashboard

Config.Name: Trusted proxy
Config.Description: Optional single proxy IP or DNS name as seen by the container. Proxy must overwrite forwarding headers; see networking documentation. || Wiki: https://github.com/Crosis47/tmodloader/wiki/Configuration#web-dashboard

Config.Name: Administrator hash file
Config.Description: WebUI only. Optional container path to an existing Argon2id credential hash file; add a matching read-only file mount. Empty uses first-run setup. || Wiki: https://github.com/Crosis47/tmodloader/wiki/Configuration#web-dashboard

Config.Name: Workshop API key file
Config.Description: WebUI only. Optional container path to a Steam API key file; add a matching read-only file mount. A key saved in the dashboard takes precedence. || Wiki: https://github.com/Crosis47/tmodloader/wiki/Configuration#web-dashboard

Config.Name: Game password file
Config.Description: Optional path inside the container; add a matching read-only file mount. Saved dashboard passwords override this in web mode. || Wiki: https://github.com/Crosis47/tmodloader/wiki/Configuration#change-the-game-password

Config.Name: Automatic runtime updates
Config.Description: 1 checks and tests runtime updates at startup. 0 retains the installed runtime. First startup always requires a download. || Wiki: https://github.com/Crosis47/tmodloader/wiki/Configuration#startup-runtime-updates

Config.Name: Runtime update channel
Config.Description: Empty follows the image channel; enter stable or preview to override. Applied at container startup. || Wiki: https://github.com/Crosis47/tmodloader/wiki/Configuration#startup-runtime-updates

Config.Name: Runtime version pin
Config.Description: Exact supported tModLoader release. Empty follows the selected channel; downgrades require a matching checkpoint. || Wiki: https://github.com/Crosis47/tmodloader/wiki/Configuration#startup-runtime-updates

Config.Name: Update free-space reserve (MiB)
Config.Description: Additional free space beyond three copies of game data required for startup update staging. || Wiki: https://github.com/Crosis47/tmodloader/wiki/Configuration#startup-runtime-updates

Config.Name: Update readiness timeout (seconds)
Config.Description: Maximum wait for the copied-world compatibility test and live startup readiness. || Wiki: https://github.com/Crosis47/tmodloader/wiki/Configuration#startup-runtime-updates

Config.Name: GitHub API token
Config.Description: Optional narrowly scoped token for release-discovery API rate limits. Not required for ordinary public downloads. Stored in container configuration; not a dashboard setting. || Wiki: https://github.com/Crosis47/tmodloader/wiki/Updates-and-Storage#startup-runtime-updates

Config.Name: Enable Dashboard
Config.Description: Enabled (1): no need to set any game settings below; leave their defaults and configure them in the dashboard. Keep Manage game settings with set to web (default). Optional deployment settings above are configured in Unraid. Disabled (0): expand Show more settings and configure the game settings in Unraid; administrator setup is skipped. || Wiki: https://github.com/Crosis47/tmodloader/wiki/Configuration#web-dashboard

Config.Name: Initial game password
Config.Description: Optional player password, separate from the administrator credential. Empty disables it. Saved dashboard password overrides this after setup. || Wiki: https://github.com/Crosis47/tmodloader/wiki/Configuration#change-the-game-password

Config.Name: Welcome message
Config.Default: A tModLoader server powered by Docker!
Config.Description: Message displayed to players when they join the server. In web mode, saved dashboard settings override this value; in env mode, Unraid controls it. || Wiki: https://github.com/Crosis47/tmodloader/wiki/Configuration#game-network-and-access

Container.Config: A tModLoader server powered by Docker!

Config.Name: Maximum players
Config.Description: Maximum simultaneous players allowed, from 1 to 255. In web mode, saved dashboard settings override this value; in env mode, Unraid controls it. || Wiki: https://github.com/Crosis47/tmodloader/wiki/Configuration#game-network-and-access

Config.Name: Server language
Config.Description: Language code for server messages, such as en-US. In web mode, saved dashboard settings override this value; in env mode, Unraid controls it. || Wiki: https://github.com/Crosis47/tmodloader/wiki/Configuration#game-network-and-access

Config.Name: Additional cheat protection
Config.Description: 0 disables Terraria’s additional cheat checks; 1 enables them. This is not authentication or a firewall. In web mode, saved dashboard settings override this value; in env mode, Unraid controls it. || Wiki: https://github.com/Crosis47/tmodloader/wiki/Configuration#runtime-and-diagnostics

Config.Name: NPC streaming range
Config.Description: Controls NPC streaming to clients, from 0 to 1000. Leave the default unless tuning network behavior. In web mode, saved dashboard settings override this value; in env mode, Unraid controls it. || Wiki: https://github.com/Crosis47/tmodloader/wiki/Configuration#runtime-and-diagnostics

Config.Name: UPnP port mapping
Config.Description: 0 disables automatic router port mapping; 1 requests it. Docker port publishing and firewall rules still need host configuration. In web mode, saved dashboard settings override this value; in env mode, Unraid controls it. || Wiki: https://github.com/Crosis47/tmodloader/wiki/Configuration#runtime-and-diagnostics

Config.Name: World name
Config.Description: Selects the world file by name. A different name may create a new world if no matching file exists. Do not include path separators. In web mode, saved dashboard settings override this value; in env mode, Unraid controls it. || Wiki: https://github.com/Crosis47/tmodloader/wiki/Configuration#world-selection-and-generation

Config.Name: New world size
Config.Description: Used only when creating a world: 1 small, 2 medium, 3 large. In web mode, saved dashboard settings override this value; in env mode, Unraid controls it. || Wiki: https://github.com/Crosis47/tmodloader/wiki/Configuration#world-selection-and-generation

Config.Name: New world evil
Config.Description: Random, Corruption, or Crimson. To change evil in the WebUI, choose an unused world name, stage the settings, and apply changes. Apply saves and stops the game, disconnects players, creates the new world, and restarts. Existing worlds are never converted; a matching name loads that world. Custom evil requires a name of at most 26 characters and seed of at most 39 characters. Special seeds and mods may generate both evils or alter generation. In web mode, saved dashboard settings override this value; in env mode, Unraid controls it. || Wiki: https://github.com/Crosis47/tmodloader/wiki/Configuration#world-selection-and-generation

Config.Name: New world seed
Config.Description: Seed used when generating a new world. Changing it does not regenerate the current world. In web mode, saved dashboard settings override this value; in env mode, Unraid controls it. || Wiki: https://github.com/Crosis47/tmodloader/wiki/Configuration#world-selection-and-generation

Config.Name: New world difficulty
Config.Description: Used when creating a world: 0 Classic, 1 Expert, 2 Master, 3 Journey. In web mode, saved dashboard settings override this value; in env mode, Unraid controls it. || Wiki: https://github.com/Crosis47/tmodloader/wiki/Configuration#world-selection-and-generation

Config.Name: Selected Workshop entries
Config.Description: Comma-separated Workshop mod IDs or collection:ID entries. Removing an entry disables it on managed startup but keeps cached downloads. In web mode, saved dashboard settings override this value; in env mode, Unraid controls it. || Wiki: https://github.com/Crosis47/tmodloader/wiki/Configuration#mods-and-workshop

Config.Name: Steam offline policy
Config.Description: use-cache allows startup with available cached mods when Steam cannot be reached. strict fails if required update/download checks fail. In web mode, saved dashboard settings override this value; in env mode, Unraid controls it. || Wiki: https://github.com/Crosis47/tmodloader/wiki/Configuration#mods-and-workshop

Config.Name: Collection expansion limit
Config.Description: Maximum items allowed while expanding Workshop collections, from 1 to 1000. Limits unexpectedly large collections. In web mode, saved dashboard settings override this value; in env mode, Unraid controls it. || Wiki: https://github.com/Crosis47/tmodloader/wiki/Configuration#mods-and-workshop

Config.Name: Download attempts
Config.Description: Maximum attempts for transient Steam Workshop download failures, from 1 to 20. In web mode, saved dashboard settings override this value; in env mode, Unraid controls it. || Wiki: https://github.com/Crosis47/tmodloader/wiki/Configuration#mods-and-workshop

Config.Name: Retry delay (seconds)
Config.Description: Time to wait between failed download attempts, from 0 to 600 seconds. In web mode, saved dashboard settings override this value; in env mode, Unraid controls it. || Wiki: https://github.com/Crosis47/tmodloader/wiki/Configuration#mods-and-workshop

Config.Name: Autosave interval (minutes)
Config.Description: Save the live world every N minutes (default: 10). 0 disables scheduled autosaves. Saves update the world in place without disconnecting players; they do not create backup archives. Save the draft, then Apply & Restart to activate a changed interval. The timer resets when the game starts. In web mode, saved dashboard settings override this value; in env mode, Unraid controls it. || Wiki: https://github.com/Crosis47/tmodloader/wiki/Configuration#backups-and-autosave

Config.Name: Autosave chat announcement
Config.Description: Chat message sent before each scheduled save. Leave empty to save silently. The autosave interval controls the schedule; 0 disables scheduled saves. Save the draft and apply to activate changes. In web mode, saved dashboard settings override this value; in env mode, Unraid controls it. || Wiki: https://github.com/Crosis47/tmodloader/wiki/Configuration#backups-and-autosave

Config.Name: Backup schedule
Config.Description: Choose disabled, minutes, every X days, daily, weekly, or monthly. Interval mode preserves the existing backup interval. Cold backups disconnect players, save, archive, and restart the game. In web mode, saved dashboard settings override this value; in env mode, Unraid controls it. || Wiki: https://github.com/Crosis47/tmodloader/wiki/Configuration#backups-and-autosave

Config.Name: Backup interval (minutes)
Config.Description: 0 disables scheduled backups. 1440 runs approximately every 24 hours. The interval resets on container start or after a manual backup. In web mode, saved dashboard settings override this value; in env mode, Unraid controls it. || Wiki: https://github.com/Crosis47/tmodloader/wiki/Configuration#backups-and-autosave

Config.Name: Back up every X days
Config.Description: Used in days mode. Each day is 24 hours. The timer resets on container startup, configuration apply, and after any backup attempt. In web mode, saved dashboard settings override this value; in env mode, Unraid controls it. || Wiki: https://github.com/Crosis47/tmodloader/wiki/Configuration#backups-and-autosave

Config.Name: Backup weekday
Config.Description: Used for weekly backups at the selected backup time and timezone. In web mode, saved dashboard settings override this value; in env mode, Unraid controls it. || Wiki: https://github.com/Crosis47/tmodloader/wiki/Configuration#backups-and-autosave

Config.Name: Backup day of month
Config.Description: Used for monthly backups. Choose 1 through 31; shorter months use their last day. In web mode, saved dashboard settings override this value; in env mode, Unraid controls it. || Wiki: https://github.com/Crosis47/tmodloader/wiki/Configuration#backups-and-autosave

Config.Name: Backup time
Config.Description: Daily, weekly, and monthly backups use this 24-hour HH:MM time. Busy or unhealthy servers defer the backup. In web mode, saved dashboard settings override this value; in env mode, Unraid controls it. || Wiki: https://github.com/Crosis47/tmodloader/wiki/Configuration#backups-and-autosave

Config.Name: Backup timezone
Config.Description: Use UTC or an IANA timezone such as America/New_York. Missing daylight-saving times shift forward; repeated times use their first occurrence. In web mode, saved dashboard settings override this value; in env mode, Unraid controls it. || Wiki: https://github.com/Crosis47/tmodloader/wiki/Configuration#backups-and-autosave

Config.Name: Backups to retain
Config.Description: Number of verified backup bundles to keep for this data directory. Cleanup runs only after a successful backup and restart; recovery originals are not pruned. In web mode, saved dashboard settings override this value; in env mode, Unraid controls it. || Wiki: https://github.com/Crosis47/tmodloader/wiki/Configuration#backups-and-autosave

Config.Name: Minimum free space (MiB)
Config.Description: Refuse a backup before stopping the game when /backups has less free space than this threshold. 1024 means 1 GiB. This is not an archive-size estimate; 0 disables the threshold. In web mode, saved dashboard settings override this value; in env mode, Unraid controls it. || Wiki: https://github.com/Crosis47/tmodloader/wiki/Configuration#backups-and-autosave

Config.Name: Restart schedule
Config.Description: Choose disabled (default), minutes, every X days, daily, weekly, or monthly. Save the draft and apply to activate changes. Busy or unhealthy servers defer the restart until ready. In web mode, saved dashboard settings override this value; in env mode, Unraid controls it. || Wiki: https://github.com/Crosis47/tmodloader/wiki/Configuration#scheduled-restarts

Config.Name: Restart interval (minutes)
Config.Description: Used in interval mode only. 0 disables interval restarts; 1440 is approximately every 24 hours. The timer resets whenever the game starts, including after backups or applying settings. In web mode, saved dashboard settings override this value; in env mode, Unraid controls it. || Wiki: https://github.com/Crosis47/tmodloader/wiki/Configuration#scheduled-restarts

Config.Name: Restart every X days
Config.Description: Used in every-X-days mode. Enter 1 through 3650; each day is exactly 24 hours. The timer resets whenever the game starts, including after backups or applying settings. It does not use the calendar time or timezone. In web mode, saved dashboard settings override this value; in env mode, Unraid controls it. || Wiki: https://github.com/Crosis47/tmodloader/wiki/Configuration#scheduled-restarts

Config.Name: Restart weekday
Config.Description: Used in weekly mode. Choose the weekday on which the restart warning begins, at the selected time in the selected timezone. In web mode, saved dashboard settings override this value; in env mode, Unraid controls it. || Wiki: https://github.com/Crosis47/tmodloader/wiki/Configuration#scheduled-restarts

Config.Name: Restart day of month
Config.Description: Used in monthly mode. Choose 1 through 31. If a month has fewer days, use its last day: 31 becomes February 28 or 29, for example. In web mode, saved dashboard settings override this value; in env mode, Unraid controls it. || Wiki: https://github.com/Crosis47/tmodloader/wiki/Configuration#scheduled-restarts

Config.Name: Restart time
Config.Description: Used for daily, weekly, and monthly schedules. Enter HH:MM in 24-hour format, such as 04:00, in the restart timezone below. The warning starts at this time; the game stops after the warning delay. In web mode, saved dashboard settings override this value; in env mode, Unraid controls it. || Wiki: https://github.com/Crosis47/tmodloader/wiki/Configuration#scheduled-restarts

Config.Name: Restart timezone
Config.Description: Used for daily, weekly, and monthly schedules. Use UTC or an IANA timezone such as America/New_York. A skipped daylight-saving time shifts forward by the clock-change gap; a repeated time runs at its first occurrence only. In web mode, saved dashboard settings override this value; in env mode, Unraid controls it. || Wiki: https://github.com/Crosis47/tmodloader/wiki/Configuration#scheduled-restarts

Config.Name: Restart warning delay (seconds)
Config.Description: Wait after the scheduled restart announcement before saving and stopping the game. Default: 60; 0 restarts immediately. This delay is separate from the Docker shutdown warning delay. In web mode, saved dashboard settings override this value; in env mode, Unraid controls it. || Wiki: https://github.com/Crosis47/tmodloader/wiki/Configuration#scheduled-restarts

Config.Name: Restart countdown warnings (seconds)
Config.Description: Comma-separated remaining times, such as 300,60,10. Warnings longer than the restart delay are skipped. Leave empty to disable countdown chat messages; the initial announcement is controlled separately. In web mode, saved dashboard settings override this value; in env mode, Unraid controls it. || Wiki: https://github.com/Crosis47/tmodloader/wiki/Configuration#scheduled-restarts

Config.Name: Restart chat announcement
Config.Default: Scheduled server restart soon. Please prepare to disconnect.
Config.Description: Chat message sent when a scheduled restart becomes due, before the warning delay. Leave empty to omit the announcement. Players will still disconnect when the game restarts. In web mode, saved dashboard settings override this value; in env mode, Unraid controls it. || Wiki: https://github.com/Crosis47/tmodloader/wiki/Configuration#scheduled-restarts

Container.Config: Scheduled server restart soon. Please prepare to disconnect.

Config.Name: Shutdown announcement
Config.Description: Chat message sent to players when Docker requests a graceful container shutdown. In web mode, saved dashboard settings override this value; in env mode, Unraid controls it. || Wiki: https://github.com/Crosis47/tmodloader/wiki/Configuration#runtime-and-diagnostics

Config.Name: Shutdown warning delay (seconds)
Config.Description: Wait after the shutdown announcement before requesting save-and-exit when Docker stops the container. Default: 3; 0 skips the delay. Keep Docker stop_grace_period longer than this delay plus the graceful shutdown timeout and shutdown overhead. Dashboard restarts and backups use their own stop flow. In web mode, saved dashboard settings override this value; in env mode, Unraid controls it. Keep Unraid Docker Stop Timeout and Extra Parameters --stop-timeout greater than shutdown delay + timeout + overhead (120 seconds by default). || Wiki: https://github.com/Crosis47/tmodloader/wiki/Configuration#runtime-and-diagnostics

Config.Name: Graceful shutdown timeout (seconds)
Config.Description: How long to wait after requesting a save-and-exit before forced termination. Keep Docker’s stop_grace_period longer than this value plus shutdown overhead. In web mode, saved dashboard settings override this value; in env mode, Unraid controls it. Keep Unraid Docker Stop Timeout and Extra Parameters --stop-timeout greater than shutdown delay + timeout + overhead (120 seconds by default). || Wiki: https://github.com/Crosis47/tmodloader/wiki/Configuration#runtime-and-diagnostics

Config.Name: Console verbosity
Config.Description: quiet reduces routine output; normal shows standard output; debug shows detailed output. Complete raw output remains in the persistent console log. In web mode, saved dashboard settings override this value; in env mode, Unraid controls it. || Wiki: https://github.com/Crosis47/tmodloader/wiki/Configuration#runtime-and-diagnostics

Config.Name: Crash replay lines
Config.Description: Number of raw console lines replayed when the game fails. 0 disables crash replay; debug already shows raw output. In web mode, saved dashboard settings override this value; in env mode, Unraid controls it. || Wiki: https://github.com/Crosis47/tmodloader/wiki/Configuration#runtime-and-diagnostics

Config.Name: Console history retention (days)
Config.Description: Remove archived console logs older than this many days. Default: 30; 0 disables age-based cleanup. The current and previous console logs and tModLoader own logs are kept. In web mode, saved dashboard settings override this value; in env mode, Unraid controls it. || Wiki: https://github.com/Crosis47/tmodloader/wiki/Configuration#runtime-and-diagnostics

Config.Name: Console history size limit (MiB)
Config.Description: Remove oldest archived console logs until history fits this budget. Default: 512; 0 disables the size limit. Current and previous console logs are separate from this budget. In web mode, saved dashboard settings override this value; in env mode, Unraid controls it. || Wiki: https://github.com/Crosis47/tmodloader/wiki/Configuration#runtime-and-diagnostics

Config.Name: Console log rotation size (MiB)
Config.Description: Rotate the current console log at this size so one long server session cannot grow it indefinitely. Default: 64. Cleanup runs at startup, rotation, and periodically while output is received. In web mode, saved dashboard settings override this value; in env mode, Unraid controls it. || Wiki: https://github.com/Crosis47/tmodloader/wiki/Configuration#runtime-and-diagnostics

Config.Name: Process priority
Config.Description: Server scheduling priority, from 0 (realtime) to 5 (idle). Lower values request higher priority; container permissions may limit this. Prefer the default unless diagnosing performance. In web mode, saved dashboard settings override this value; in env mode, Unraid controls it. || Wiki: https://github.com/Crosis47/tmodloader/wiki/Configuration#runtime-and-diagnostics

Config.Name: Freeze time
Config.Description: Who can control freeze time in a Journey world: 0 locked, 1 host only, 2 everyone. In web mode, saved dashboard settings override this value; in env mode, Unraid controls it. || Wiki: https://github.com/Crosis47/tmodloader/wiki/Configuration#journey-permissions
